# CS-301 Database Management Systems — Syllabus

Course code: CS-301. Credits: 4. Semester: V. Offered by the Department of Computer Science.

## Unit 1: Introduction and the ER Model
Purpose of database systems, data independence, the three-schema architecture, entity-relationship (ER) diagrams, keys and participation constraints.

## Unit 2: Relational Model and SQL
Relational algebra, tuple relational calculus, SQL data definition and data manipulation, joins, nested queries, views and integrity constraints.

## Unit 3: Normalization
Functional dependencies, Armstrong's axioms, closure of attributes, decomposition, first normal form (1NF), second normal form (2NF), third normal form (3NF) and Boyce-Codd normal form (BCNF). Lossless join and dependency preservation.

## Unit 4: Transactions and Concurrency Control
ACID properties, schedules, conflict serializability, two-phase locking, timestamp ordering, deadlock handling and recovery with write-ahead logging.

## Unit 5: Indexing and Hashing
Ordered indices, B+ tree index files, static and dynamic hashing, and query processing basics.

## Evaluation
Two mid-semester tests (20 marks each), lab work (20 marks) and an end-semester examination (40 marks). The minimum attendance requirement is 75 percent.
